newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO steady to firm on buying support.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO steady to firm on buying support.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Thursday were expected to stay supported by a local trader who has recently soaked up December barrels, traders said.
Traders expected prices to exceed $123-$125 per tonne for 180-cst quoted on Wednesday.
Late Thursday, a trader was seen offering January barrels at $125 per tonne. But no bids were seen.

They said demand from China remained steady. Chinese bids were heard at $7.50 per tonne over Singapore spot quotes, c+f southern China for January delivery. But offers were over $9.00 per tonne premiums.
They said South Korean barrels were offered at $1.50-premium on free-on-board Ulsan basis for early January lifting.
Freight costs between China and South Korea were pegged at a high level of $8.00 per tonne.
Swaps levels hardly moved. January were quoted at $120.50/$121.75, almost unchanged from Wednesday's indications.
